- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast for next 5–7 days at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.3) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% to next 7–10 days.
- Model consistently overestimates mean price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; use 30-day moving average as baseline and adjust down 2–5% if sentiment < 0.2.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 30-day MA), model often ignores it; reduce forecast by 3–6% for next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.8) and price is rising, model often overfits to recent momentum; cap forecast at 1–2% below 3-day moving average of true values.
